questions.question: What is the core mechanism of self-attention in a Transformer?
choices: It uses a recurrent loop to process tokens sequentially
Each token generates a Query, Key, and Value vector to compute attention scores against all other tokens
It compares each token to a fixed external memory bank
It only looks at the previous three tokens in the sequence
questions.explanation: Self-attention computes Q, K, V vectors for each token, then calculates attention scores using the dot product of Q and K, scaled and passed through softmax, to weight the Value vectors.

questions.question: Why is the scaling factor √(d_k) used when computing attention scores?
choices: To speed up matrix multiplication by reducing dimensions
To prevent dot products from growing too large, which would push softmax into regions with tiny gradients
To make the model use less memory during training
To ensure all attention weights are exactly 0 or 1
questions.explanation: As the dimension d_k grows, dot products tend to increase in magnitude, pushing softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. Dividing by √d_k keeps the variance stable and gradients healthy.

questions.question: In the self-attention formula Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / √d_k) · V, what does the softmax operation do?
choices: It converts the attention scores into a probability distribution that sums to 1
It removes all negative values from the score matrix
It normalizes the input tokens to have zero mean
It selects only the single highest-scoring token
questions.explanation: Softmax converts raw attention scores into a probability distribution — each row sums to 1 — so the weighted sum of Value vectors represents a mixture of information from all tokens, weighted by relevance.
